skill: Nonlinear Equations In One Variable And Systems Of Equations In Two Variables
prompt: What value of $x$ satisfies the equation $\frac{(12)}{(x-7)}-\frac{6}{(x-7)}=\frac{2}{3}$?
explanation: Combining the fractions on the left side yields $\frac{12-6}{x-7}=\frac{2}{3}$, which simplifies to $\frac{6}{x-7}=\frac{2}{3}$. Cross-multiplying gives $6 \cdot 3 = 2(x-7)$, so $18=2x-14$. Adding $14$ to both sides gives $32=2x$, and dividing by $2$ yields $x=16$.
